== Biography ==
Thomas Glasgow was christened on 21 February 1675 in Linlithgow, Linlithgowshire, Scotland, the son of [[Glasgow-1105|John Glasgow]] and [[Eastone-3|Agnes Eastone]].<ref name="Baptism">"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, ''FamilySearch'' (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4C-P4L : 16 September 2021), Thomas Glesgow, 1675.</ref>

He married [[Duncan-16665|Jean Duncan]] on 4 May 1701 in Linlithgow.<ref name="Marriage">Marriage date from family records; primary source from the Linlithgow Old Parish Registers needs to be located and attached.</ref> Thomas and Jean had at least two sons confirmed in the Linlithgowshire area:

* [[Glasgow-1244|A son]], whose name is not given in the indexed record, was christened on 2 July 1704 in the neighboring parish of Uphall, Linlithgowshire.<ref name="Son1704">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, ''FamilySearch'' (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ48-MZ7 : 16 September 2021), Thomas Glasghow in entry for Glasghow, 1704.</ref>
* [[Glasgow-1241|Philip Glasgow]] was christened on 21 October 1711, back in the parish of Linlithgow.<ref name="Philip1711">"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, ''FamilySearch'' (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ48-S78 : 16 September 2021), Thomas Glesgow in entry for Philips Glesgow, 1711.</ref>

Although the 1711 christening record for Philip omits his mother's name, the established marriage of his father to Jean Duncan in the same parish makes her the certain mother. The omission was likely a simple oversight by the parish clerk.

The preceding claim of certain maternity is not adopted by this review. An omitted mother and a proposed household identification do not establish Jean Duncan as this child’s certain mother; retain the attribution as uncertain until an identifying record resolves it.

The date and place of Thomas's death are not yet known, but he was alive as of October 1711.

== Research Notes ==
=== Uphall household review, 23 October 2026 ===

The newly inspected Findmypast transcripts establish Thomas Glasgow and Jean Duncan’s Linlithgow banns on 30 March 1701 (groom a servant; witnesses James Craw and William Duncan) and marriage on 4 May 1701. The banns leave both residences as question marks. A third Linlithgow register index names the same couple in 1701 without a day. These are related register entries, not three independent family identifications. Two Findmypast FamilySearch-derived entries name Philip Glasgow, male, baptised 3 June 1711 at Uphall, father Thomas Glasgow and mother Jean Duncan. They corroborate the maintained Scottish child account and do not identify a Mary. The older Mary label is an editorial inconsistency, not a second contemporary child. The separate family citation giving 21 October 1711/Linlithgow remains an unresolved index discrepancy: its underlying page was inaccessible and the present search did not find it. Duplicate transcriptions do not supply independent testimony. The 1675 child’s existing John-1105 father assessment stays 98%, scoped to that child. Philip-1241’s complete father-profile assessment is now 72%; the Clarkson adult’s John-1105 hypothesis is 30%. 30% is a subjective assessment of the complete Clarkson-adult → John-1105 proposition. Two identity bridges remain unproved: the 1675 child to the Duncan groom, and the Duncan father to the Clarkson groom. No widowhood, remarital status, age, trade or parent is given in the inspected marriage transcripts. Jean’s death is not established. An unrecorded younger local Thomas remains a serious alternative; Thomas-1311 (1666) and Thomas-3091 (1663) are older compatible rivals. The 1679 Carstairs/Spence groom is not an established identity for this adult. The unverified 1766 memorial contributes no weight. The 1715 Edinburgh citation is excluded from the supporting sequence. Both Thomas accounts remain separate and no biological or profile merge is made.

The dated review above supersedes earlier statements that the 1701 marriage was only family information, that the 1711 child was Mary, or that the 1715 Edinburgh child supports the Uphall sequence. Other earlier evidence and unresolved alternatives remain below.

=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

The existing father [[Glasgow-1105]] is assessed at 98% (proved). Thomas’s 1675 Linlithgow index names John Glasgow and Agnes Eastone. The same parental couple recurs in the existing John household, including the 1671 child, giving a specific record-defined father identification.

Recorded 1675 child98%; the2/21 February discrepancy and later Duncan/Clarkson Thomas identities remain separate. Original uninspected.

Next useful test: Test Thomas’s later adult identities independently of the explicit child parentage.

Source basis already held: [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4C-P4L Thomas Glesgow, Linlithgow 1675: child/parent index VQ4C-P4L]. No new original inspected; no new father attached.


=== Selected uncertain family — 16 October 2026 ===

Select Thomas [[Glasgow-1242]] as the uncertain working father of Philip [[Glasco-146]]. The preferred model uses [[Glasco-146]] as the elder Dublin watchmaker account, retaining the 1711 Scottish child [[Glasgow-1241]] as a separate possible account of the same man. That child’s Uphall index names father Thomas; his existing research already retains the elder watchmaker as a compatible adult identity. The [[Glasco-146]] account has the Christ Church Lane watchmaking association in 1752, an estimated birth about 1715 and a younger Philip in its tree family, which suit that provisional elder role. The four-year difference from the 1711 baptism is between a record and an unsupported estimate, not a concrete identity conflict. This materialises the existing Scottish candidate at low confidence; it does not prove migration or two distinct elder Philips.

The Dublin records name no Scottish parents, birthplace or apprenticeship, so the Scottish child and elder watchmaker may be different men. The fresh [[Glasco-146]] biography itself mixes the 1752 watchmaker with junior notices of 1765,1768 and 1770. Its c.1715 birth and the c.1740 birth of [[Glasco-147]] are tree estimates, not evidence selecting a generation. If [[Glasco-146]] instead represents the junior, the elder Philip is an alternative father-generation placement and the Thomas link would need revision; no competing father is attached alongside it. The elder placement is a preferred working interpretation of the profile’s trade/address and family structure, not a claim that every event in that biography belongs to him. The junior’s 1765 unnamed-wife death,1768 Teresa Plunkett marriage and reported 1770 death remain with the younger documentary account [[Glasgow-3932]]. [[Glasco-147]] is a strongly supported duplicate account of that younger man, but its quoted 1772 younger/inventory wording was not independently rechecked here and establishes neither the estimated birth nor a newly verified father clause; a grant date is not a death date. No merge, spouse transfer or new child attachment follows. Catherine Mangan is called [[Glasco-146]]’s mother in its prose but spouse in its structured family; the 1750 report describes the elder’s bride only as the widow Mangan, and the 1760 report gives no forename. Neither record proves maternity. Preserve the existing Mangan/Braccan and younger-parent fields as qualified leads; do not add a mother for [[Glasco-146]]. The father Thomas is common to the retained 1711 child records, while the 3 June Uphall versus 21 October Linlithgow Philip entries and their maternal readings remain unreconciled; Jean Duncan is not transferred as [[Glasco-146]]’s mother. The 1777 probate/court occurrence does not establish survival after 1772. The local elder account uses 1772 as an uncertain death year through the selected identity, retaining the old after 1772 value and all junior events in the comparison.

Thomas’s own existing parents and Duncan/Clarkson identity alternatives retain their grades. === Selected uncertain family — 16 October 2026 ===

The Clarkson adult1226 is now selected under the same uncertain parents through possible identity with this child/adult account. This is not proof of two Thomas sons. The 1675 child parentage and the identification of the later Duncan household remain distinct questions. Select John [[Glasgow-1105]] and Agnes Eastone-3 as the uncertain working parents of Thomas [[Glasgow-1226]], the father with Catherine Clarkson/Classon at Uphall from 1717 and Livingston by 1730. This selects possible identity with their named Linlithgow child Thomas [[Glasgow-1242]] of 1675, while retaining both profile accounts. That child would be about 42 at the 1717 Margaret entry and about 60 at the 1735 Hellen entry: later fatherhood, but chronologically possible. The existing Glasgow-1242 account also represents a Thomas/Jean Duncan household at Uphall in 1704. Recurring Thomas name, the same Uphall parish and a plausible succession of households provide a more specific route than the removed Kilbirnie-minister parents. The 1675 parent clause belongs directly to the child account; transferring it to the Clarkson adult depends wholly on the uncertain identity.

The 1675 child, the Duncan adult and the Clarkson adult may represent one, two or three men. There is no inspected age, occupation, marriage, widowhood or probate bridge. The 1701 Duncan marriage is reported family information, not a newly inspected register. No death of Jean, remarriage to Catherine or overlap resolution is invented. The differing Philip 1711 dates in the Thomas research compilation and the Glasgow-1242 biography, and the omission of a mother in the latter’s indexed child, do not establish a continuous Duncan household or certain maternity. They are not two independent confirmations. Catherine’s indexed surname variants remain as recorded. The before 1700 boundary for the Clarkson adult and the 2/21 February 1675 date discrepancy in the child account remain unchanged. The 1666 St Cuthbert’s Thomas-1311, child of Alexander and Issobell Anderson, remains a compatible identity alternative, albeit with fatherhood at about 51–69 in 1717–1735. His possible identification with the Edinburgh writer whose testament was indexed in 1691 is unproved and cannot be used to exclude him. The retained 1766 grave link is an unverified namesake comparison, not an established death for the Clarkson adult. The 1663 Thomas-3091 and an otherwise unrecorded local Thomas also remain possible. No identity merge or live attachment is performed. *   '''Uncertain Record:''' A record exists for the christening of a [[Glasgow-1243|Thomas Glasgow]], son of a Thomas Glasgow, on 15 June 1715 in Edinburgh.<ref name="Thomas1715">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", , FamilySearch ({{FamilySearch Record |   F3BT-24V}} : 11 February 2020), Thomas Glasgow in entry for Thomas Glasgow, 1715.</ref> It is uncertain if this is the same family. The location is in a different county (Midlothian), and the mother is not named. This could be a different Thomas Glasgow family entirely. Further research, such as looking for land or kirk session records, is needed to determine if this family moved from Linlithgow to Edinburgh between 1711 and 1715.

*   Search for death or burial records for Thomas Glasgow (after Oct 1711) and [[Duncan-16665|Jean Duncan]] in the parish registers of Linlithgow and surrounding areas.
